chapter: Young players, Coltrane and the avant-garde
title: Coltrane knew what he was doing; his practicing
summary: Ridley and Sam say avant-garde players missed Coltrane's method, which belongs in schools, and he practiced constantly.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: But you see, it seems to me like the mark of any kind of musician should--they might have had,--see I think you know, a point I've always felt too, the idea that a lot of these so called avant garde or freedom musicians completely missed the boat on Coltrane . if they had any kind of talent and they been developing their ears, they should have been able to hear that extra--an alyze it, realize what he was doing.

Because you played with Trane and I got a chance to play with him too, you could hear that stuff. When he be playing all them secondary dominants you'd be-- because some of them--it was a groove to play...And the way he would just be putting all them substitutions on top of that stuff--I could hear where he was going with that stuff; and that stuff was mean, you know. And you

knew, but you get with some of them other cats and it would just be like a matter of sound effects, you know, just a little ole mixing. Just like you say, that...random bullshit, you know,...they play, but that man knew what he was doing--

He knew exactly what he was doing and it wasn't no put on or nothing, man, this man knew exactly musically what he was doing. And that's what he practiced and that's how he came up with all that stuff. See, that stuff should be in school,man, all of his stuff should be in school. Now, I don't know if his wife, his first wife, you know,--
I don't know if she still have all that stuff, if she got it man, if she do have it, man, then she should hand it over to ah, to some school man, because it's very important.
Yeah. It's very important that--that the kids should should have that, you know. I don't know, he probably had some other stuff when he married again, you know, to uh--

To Alice. Yeah. But his first wife... house,...out there too seeing her you know. He brought my whole that thing out, man and that cleared up--I said, "Jesus Christ, man, how can this man play all this stuff man."
Yeah, I saw that, he showed me that, that that ...
So now, now now, I understood what he was doing before you see I wasn't sure. You know. But when I saw that, man, oh man, this guy here, boy, is, whew (laughter).
And see how he had figured all that stuff out, too, and had it right on the...he used to hang up there and right on the wall --
He'd be sitting up there looking at it and he just goes through it all, whew, this guy here.

And he practiced, this guy practiced all the time, man. Even, you know, when, on his off days he didn't have no off days. He played, he practiced just as hard as when--and then sometimes, man, on intermission, man, he would be back, in the back in the dressing room, you know. He had some stuff man. Practicing...try it.
